benchmarks.name: ImageNet (ILSVRC) top-5 error
benchmarks.creator: Fei-Fei Li and collaborators (Princeton, Stanford); ILSVRC organizers

human_baseline.note: Andrej Karpathy estimated in 2014 he could reach 5.1% error with concentrated effort; about 10 lab members reached roughly 12 to 13% with less effort.

points.model: Linear SVM on HoG and LBP features (NEC-UIUC)

benchmarks.notes: Lower is better: top-5 error counts images whose correct label was missing from a model's five guesses. Values are winning ILSVRC classification entries (2010 and 2011 converted from reported top-5 accuracy of 71.8% and 74.2%). ResNet (Dec 2015) was first to win below the 5.1% human estimate; organizers said 2017 would be their last competition because this benchmark was effectively solved. Later studies estimated over 6% of validation labels, its answer key, are wrong, which limits further meaningful gains.

benchmarks.creator: Fei-Fei Li and collaborators; ILSVRC organizers

points.model: ResNeXt-101 32x48d, weakly supervised on Instagram hashtags

benchmarks.notes: Top-1 accuracy counts images whose single best guess was right. Record claims come from arXiv paper abstracts, dated by first arXiv submission; extra training data varies by entry (Instagram, JFT). Papers with Code archives could not be reached when this record was compiled, so this series samples widely cited records and is not a complete leaderboard. Top-1 has no agreed human baseline; label noise, meaning wrong answers in the test set, of roughly 6 to 10% (per later audits) caps meaningful accuracy.
